member.name: P:Prowl.Runtime.SceneReferenceResolver.LinkedOut
member.summary:
The objects this resolver linked out rather than serialized, in the order it met them.
Linking out is right for a copy, which lands back in the same scene. It is a loss for a prefab asset, which cannot hold a scene reference at all and will read the link back as null. The resolver is the only place that knows it happened, so it records it and lets the caller decide whether that is worth saying anything about.

member.name: P:Prowl.Runtime.Window.ContentScale
member.summary:
Physical-to-logical pixel ratio for the window's current display.
On Windows, resolves glfwGetWindowContentScale via the native GLFW context to capture the system DPI factor (e.g. 1.25 at 125%). This is needed because FramebufferSize / Size only reflects the ratio when the process is per-monitor DPI-aware; if DPI awareness failed at startup the OS virtualises the framebuffer (fb == win) and the ratio collapses to 1.
On macOS and Linux the GLFW proc address is not reachable via this path, so we fall back to FramebufferSize / Size which is always correct on those platforms (Retina: 3024 fb / 1512 points = 2; 1× monitor: 1).

member.name: T:Prowl.Runtime.OpenXRSession
member.summary:
One OpenXR instance and session rendering through Graphite's Vulkan device.
The instance comes first, before the device exists, since the device is made with the Vulkan extensions and on the GPU the runtime names. The session follows on . Frame waits, events, locating and input run on the main thread. Frame begin, the swapchain images and frame end run on Graphite's render thread around the frame's submission, holding the graphics queue's lock, since the runtime may use that queue in them.

member.name: T:Prowl.Runtime.XR
member.summary:
Headset rendering and tracking through OpenXR.
While running, the first perspective with no target texture and a draws both eyes into the headset in one stereo view, using its transform as the head, and the window or Game View shows one eye. Put a on the camera so the head moves it, under a parent that places the play area in the world. The headset paces the frame loop while it shows frames, so VSync and are set aside meanwhile.
The graphics device has to be made for the headset, so set before the window opens.

member.name: T:Prowl.Vector.RectTransform
member.summary: A component that stores anchor, pivot, and size information for 2D UI layout. It is a standalone component (not a subclass), required by every UI element; rotation, scale and Z come from the GameObject's regular Transform.

remarks.para: The UI coordinate system is +Y up: anchors, pivots and all grow upward, so increasing AnchoredPosition.Y moves an element toward the top of the screen.

Anchors define how the element's edges attach to its parent rect. Values are normalized (0-1): (0,0) is bottom-left, (1,1) is top-right. When == , the element has a fixed size controlled by . When they differ, the element stretches to fill the anchor range and acts as a padding offset.
Pivot is the local origin of the element (0-1). (0,0) is bottom-left, (1,1) is top-right, (0.5, 0.5) is center.

member.name: F:Prowl.Vector.RectTransform._anchorMax
member.summary: The maximum anchor point (upper-right corner of the anchor rectangle).

member.summary: The pivot point of the element, in normalized coordinates (0-1). (0.5, 0.5) means the center.

member.name: F:Prowl.Vector.RectTransform._sizeDelta
member.summary: When the anchors are together, this represents the width and height of the rect. When the anchors are apart, this is the amount added to the anchor-defined size.

member.name: P:Prowl.Vector.Transform.LocalToWorldMatrix
member.summary: World matrix of this transform. Lazily cached: it only rebuilds when this transform's changes or an ancestor's world matrix changes, so an unmoving object walks its ancestor chain doing cheap version comparisons instead of rebuilding matrices. Every rebuild bumps so descendants know to invalidate. Not thread-safe: transforms are expected to be read on a single thread per frame.

member.name: T:RequireComponentAttribute
member.summary: Specifies that a GameObject must have certain components in addition to the one where this attribute is applied.
member.remarks:
When this attribute is used on a component, the Prowl Game Engine will automatically add the required components to the GameObject if they are not already present. This ensures that the component has all its dependencies met.
This attribute can only be applied to classes (typically components deriving from Component).
